title: 2026 FBS local radio flagships (two-engine compilation)
scope: All 138 FBS programs (part 1: Power 4 + independents; part 2: Group of Five + rebuilt Pac-12)
licensing_note: Citable affiliate facts only; no audio embedded; station- and school-authorized destinations only.
completeness: Two-engine compilation, cross-checked: part 1 (P4 + independents, as of 2026-09-08) and part 2 (G5 + rebuilt Pac-12, compiled through 2026-03-31 with current-season source spot-checks). Cross-check samples agreed on 8 of 10 teams; Michigan's flagship was corrected to WXYT-FM and Alabama's co-flagship structure recorded. One medium-confidence record (fiu).

national_context.industry_overview: Multimedia rights across the Division I Football Bowl Subdivision remain heavily consolidated among corporate aggregators managing both terrestrial syndication and proprietary streaming environments.

Learfield.power_4_share: Over 60% of SEC, Big Ten, Big 12, and ACC institutions
Learfield.distribution_platform: The Varsity Network App, SiriusXM, and regional radio syndication networks

Playfly Sports.power_4_share: Approximately 25% of major FBS properties including Penn State, Auburn, LSU, Michigan State, Nebraska, USC, and Virginia
Playfly Sports.distribution_platform: School-dedicated mobile apps, regional station networks, Audacy/iHeart partnership stations

JMI Sports.power_4_share: Selective high-value footprints including Kentucky, Pittsburgh, and Clemson (Clemson Athletic Network), alongside joint venture operations (Georgia Bulldog Sports Marketing)
JMI Sports.distribution_platform: Regional terrestrial affiliates and regional digital platforms

in_house_independent.power_4_share: Unique institutional models including BYU Broadcasting (BYU) and Fighting Irish Media (Notre Dame)
in_house_independent.distribution_platform: Institutional terrestrial stations, KSL NewsRadio, NBC digital distribution, and SiriusXM
